items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: So, the first job we got together was the three of us. It was him, Walter Nelson on the guitar, and myself on the drums.

ctx.x: What sort of date was this? Huh? What date was this about?

Oh, that was around in the 1940s. Yeah, in the 1940s, because I was living across the street at the time, at 825 North Galvestre. And the first job that, after he found out that I was playing that good, Herbert Moran, one of our old time trumpet men, he was a wonderful jazz man on the trumpet. He left Chicago and came back home. And he heard me play. He said, Joe, he said, why don't you try to stick with the drums? I said, well, if I'm playing that good, I said, I don't mind sticking with it, but if I'm bad, I…
Yes. Would that be the Parisian Room?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: So it was Hubert Moran on trumpet, Walter Nelson on guitar and me on drums.

ctx.x: And after he had heard me, he told me about joining up with him and Foster Lewis. Him and Foster, what they call him, Foster Stan. But it was Foster Stan and his brother dude had their own band. And so when they got jobs where we used to take off, you know, get off them nights and go play the job and come back and finish our work. So he told me, he gave me good advice. He said, you keep up. He said, you got a little, a little bit to learn yet. So after I got married, well, I had given up music because the…

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: My name was Herb, Walter Nelson, and we had one of Lawrence's other cousins that played piano.

ctx.x: So I sold my outfit I had. Yeah. So after I got married and moved down here, I was over across the street at 825. Yeah. Well that was during the days of Mo Rambles, Mo Rambles, who had Mo Rambles, I know who heard of him. Oh yeah. The trumpet player. Well Walter Nelson, he's down here at the Piku's place, he plays steel guitar. Yeah.
